topic: Why the US penny costs more to make than its value

script.title: US penny costs more to make than it's worth – the hidden loss
script.hook: Why does a one‑cent coin lose money on every mint?

scenes.text: Why does a one‑cent coin lose money on every mint?

motion_action.headline: Why does a one‑cent coin lose money?

scenes.text: The copper‑zinc alloy costs about three cents per penny.
Material cost has risen faster than the coin’s face value.

motion_action.label: Penny material cost vs face value

scenes.text: Since 2010, the mint’s average cost climbed to two and a half cents.
A 2019 Treasury report flagged the loss as a budgeting concern.
Why not just stop making them?

motion_action.result_headline: Congress debated eliminating the penny in 2011

scenes.text: The Mint argues the penny supports charitable rounding programs.
But those programs only offset a fraction of the production loss.
If the penny vanished, the Treasury could save roughly a hundred million dollars each year.
Now you know why the penny is a loss:

script.loop_transition_text: Now you know why the penny is a loss:
script.description:
